metadata.case_name: CHONG CHI CHING v. SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE (FOR AND ON BEHALF OF THE GOVERNMENT OF THE HKSAR) AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: customer service officer, employed by the HKSAR Government on a non-civil servant contract, working at the Government’s integrated call centre ("1823" call centre)

source: 1st MRI ... showed desiccation of L4/5 intervertebral disc and mild prolapse (PID) of L4/5 disc.
Both orthopaedic experts agreed that P suffered from soft tissue injury of back with prolapsed intervertebral disc L4/5
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

source: Both orthopaedic experts agreed that P suffered from soft tissue injury of back with prolapsed intervertebral disc L4/5
After the accident P was admitted to Accident and Emergency Department of Yan Chai Hospital, Tsuen Wan ("YCH"). There was tenderness over her low back region and x-ray showed no bone fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

source: Both doctors agreed about the diagnosis of P being adjustment disorder with depressed mood; the adjustment disorder was mainly caused by the accident and is consistent with the injury
According to the medical report prepared by Dr Sham Kwan Ho of the Department of Psychiatry dated 20 May 2013, P was diagnosed to have depressive disorder.

manifestations.description: radiating pain to right lower limb ("lightning pain shooting down her right lower limb 4 to 5 times a week")
numbness and weakness of right lower limb, particularly the two toes on the lateral side, calf and the back of her thigh
decrease in power of both lower limbs, more marked on right side
sensational loss in bilateral lower limbs
drop-foot occurred suddenly (resulting in a fall on 27 June 2012)
reduced mobility; required walking stick, wheelchair and walking aids at times; difficulty walking
reduced work efficiency; would need frequent rest after prolonged sitting ("She would need frequent rest after one hour of work")
low mood, irritability, poor concentration, poor sleep and social withdrawal
lost sense of hearing and felt headache and nausea during the second epidural injection process

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at Accident and Emergency Department of Yan Chai Hospital on 24 December 2009; given pain-killer and discharged same date
source: After the accident P was admitted to Accident and Emergency Department of Yan Chai Hospital, Tsuen Wan ("YCH"). There was tenderness over her low back region and x-ray showed no bone fracture. She was given pain-killer and was discharged home against medical advice on the same date.

treatments_received.treatment: consultations with private doctor Dr Tse Chun Man (4 occasions) and government clinic in Kwun Tong (9 occasions)
source: P had consulted a private doctor, Dr Tse Chun Man, on 4 occasions and government clinic in Kwun Tong on 9 occasions, during the period between 29 December 2009 and 26 April 2011 to relieve pain and discomfort.

treatments_received.treatment: treatment by private Chinese bone-setter Lai Sing Wah on 5 March 2010 (treated with plaster)
source: On 5 March 2010, P attended a private Chinese bone-setter, Lai Sing Wah (黎星華跌打醫局) for her back pain and she was treated with plaster.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy in UCH from 2 March 2010 to 21 June 2011 (9 sessions) and additional sessions in UCH and KH in 2011; private physiotherapy from January 2014 (claimed 20 sessions)
source: According to records, P received physiotherapy in UCH from 2 March 2010 to 21 June 2011 for 9 sessions of treatment. She also attended a number of sessions of physiotherapy treatment in UCH and KH in 2011. From January 2014 onwards, P undertook 20 sessions of physiotherapy from a private institution, Su & Huber Advanced Physiotherapy and Spinal Pain Centre for a sum of $9,000.

treatments_received.treatment: 1st epidural steroid injection on 2 September 2011 (pain partially improved)
source: On 2 September 2011, P was given epidural injection ("1st injection") and her pain partially improved and she was able to walk with a frame.

treatments_received.treatment: 2nd epidural steroid injection on 17 September 2013 (procedure stopped due to adverse reaction; hospitalization)
source: On 17 September 2013, P received 2nd Epidural Steroid Injection ("2nd injection") in UCH. It was about 2 years after the 1st injection. During the 2nd injection process, she felt drastic increase in pressure in skull and the injection stopped. She lost the sense of hearing and felt headache and nausea. She was hospitalized and was discharged on 18 September 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: inpatient admission and rehabilitation at UCH and transfer to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation (Aug 2011 period)
source: On 8 August 2011, P was discharged from UCH and was transferred to Kowloon Hospital ("KH") for rehabilitation.

According to the medical report prepared by Dr Fung Pui Man of the Department of Rehabilitation of KH dated 14 June 2012, P had been assessed by clinical psychologist with clinical impression of chronic pain disorder with signified impairment in functioning due to pain. She was not able to walk on admission but later could walk with aids and two assistants for a few steps.

treatments_received.treatment: psychiatric treatment and follow-ups (18 times between 2 March 2012 and 8 January 2013) and outpatient psychiatric follow-up
source: She received psychiatric treatment for 18 times in psychiatric department of UCH between 2 March 2012 and 8 January 2013.
She was arranged to attend regular psychiatric follow-ups.

treatments_future.treatment: ongoing psychiatric treatment (public sector) for around 2 years anticipated by one expert; possible further sessions to taper medication
source: In view of the relatively mild degree of her functional impairment from a psychiatric perspective, apart from receiving treatment in private sector, Dr Ho thought that P could continue to receive the psychiatric treatment provided in the public sector. The duration of further treatment would depend on her progress. In view of her residual symptoms, Dr Ho thought that she would likely need a further period of such treatments for at least 2 years.
Dr Law opined that P should be seen for another 6 sessions so that the medications can be gradually tapered off.

losses.description: stayed home most of the time; on average she saw her friends and her mother once a month; social withdrawal

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: used to enjoy playing guitar in a band and dancing (premorbid activities) but was no longer able to participate as before
reduced work efficiency; would need frequent rest after prolonged sitting; mild impairment of tolerance, adaptive ability and efficiency at work
